improvements.title: Make the NSC gateway actually non-reentrant: atomic try-enter at the dispatcher, Busy refusal, source-invariant test (LSB-023 class)
improvements.threat: A hostile NS image (NS is untrusted by design) installs an NS-targeted ISR (USB OTG, NS SysTick, any NS IRQ) that calls a second NSC veneer while the secure thread is blocked for up to 120 s in confirm()/enter_pin() inside a sign or unlock handler. Under ARMv8-M, NS exceptions preempt secure thread-mode code; AIRCR.PRIS only orders S above NS. The nested handler runs on top of the outer one: it wipes-and-refills the shared `static mut SIGN_SNAP_BUF` (and the pixel-UI screen tail carved out of the same static), can zeroize `master_secret` via CMD_LOCK mid-handler, raise the page-123 floor via OFFCHAIN_SYNC behind the outer dialog, or paint a second dialog that consumes the user's chord. This is exactly Ledger LSB-023 (host mutates signing parameters after display, before signature) and the BitBox pre-setup hostile-host class.
improvements.proposal: Replace `HandlerGuard::enter()` (unconditional fetch_add) with `HandlerGuard::try_enter()` doing `compare_exchange(0, 1)`; call it ONCE at the chokepoint — the start of every `cmse-nonsecure-entry` veneer and the QEMU `dispatch` — and return a new `NscStatus::Busy` on failure before any argument is read. Keep the depth semantics for SysTick (`handler_is_busy`). Additionally wrap the short handlers that today run unguarded (cmd_lock, cmd_is_unlocked, cmd_get_remaining, cmd_pin_attempt_log) under the same chokepoint so LOCK cannot land inside a live sign. Add a `main_sau_pure_tests`/`source_invariants` test asserting every `extern "cmse-nonsecure-entry" fn` body begins with the try-enter, and a QEMU e2e that issues a second mailbox command while a sign is parked in confirm() and asserts Busy + unchanged outer signature. Document the audited guarantee in threat-model.md as 'no NSC call is serviced while a trusted-UI dialog is pending'.
improvements.rationale: The inventory and threat-model credit `HandlerGuard`/`HANDLER_DEPTH` with 'non-reentrancy', but the code only counts depth; nothing refuses. Every per-handler TOCTOU defence (snapshot buffer, sender binding, display↔commit sentinel) assumes a single live handler, and `SIGN_SNAP_BUF` is a `static mut` shared by all three sign handlers through `addr_of_mut!` — a nested entry creates two live `&mut` into it (UB) and the LSB-023 shape where bytes change between render and sign. Ledger's lesson is that the guard must live in the dispatcher, not in each cmd_*; Trezor treats an out-of-contract smcall as fatal rather than ambiguous. The fix is one CAS and one status code.

improvements.title: Time-domain FI/SCA jitter at the NSC boundary: glitch-detecting wait_random at veneer entry/exit plus a per-NSC-call 'session delay' re-sample (Trezor RDI)
improvements.threat: The NSC call is the one host-visible phase marker: a host that times its own HID frame can align a glitch (clock/voltage/EM) or power/EM trace on the secure handler's first instructions — the PIN-verified sentinel read, pointer validation, entry_point compare, sender binding — with cycle-stable offsets. pq1 has double-compute/CFI on signing and a power-domain consumption mask (dilution unmeasured), but nothing in the time domain between NS->S entry and the first sentinel check.
improvements.proposal: (1) Call `fi::wait_random()` (the existing pqsigner-fi double-counter loop that halts on `i+j != wait`) as the first statement of every veneer after the USB-01 try-enter and immediately before each veneer's return. (2) Add a Trezor-style RDI: the S-only 1 ms tick (TIM2 or SysTick) busy-waits `drbg_byte() + session_delay` cycles; `session_delay` is re-sampled on every NSC entry and on every trusted-UI button event (the two host-visible phase markers). Source bytes from `rng_strong` with a budget so the #802 SysTick-entropy drain is not worsened (use a ChaCha DRBG reseeded from TRNG, as Trezor does, and make lock-contention a hard error rather than a constant). (3) Measure the added latency with `make test-key-speed` and pin the new baselines.
improvements.rationale: The primitive already exists and is proven glitch-detecting (pqsigner-fi/src/lib.rs:129-155) but is wired only around the crypto verify; threat-model.md:321 lists the sentinel as 'Planned'. Random per-call jitter forces a glitcher to search a window instead of hitting an offset, and the session term defeats averaging across calls. Cheap, orthogonal to the consumption mask, and lands on the exact boundary that the host controls.

improvements.title: Program MSPLIM in the FSBL and the secure world so any stack overflow is a deterministic fault, not silent corruption
improvements.threat: The FSBL stack is bounded by frame-sum (10,372 of 16,384 B) with no call-graph proof and no hardware limit; the secure world runs attacker-shaped parsers (ERC-7730, EIP-712, multiSend, typed-call ABI) on the same MSP with no limit either. A deeper-than-expected path driven by a hostile companion payload overflows into .bss/.data below the stack (the measurement code's data in the FSBL; `static mut` handler state and the sign snapshot in the secure image) silently. The FSBL already hit exactly this (two 8 KB manifest copies peaked main at ~24.7 KB) and only found it by inspection.
improvements.proposal: Set MSPLIM_S = stack_base + 256 B guard as the first instruction of `main` in both `fsbl/src/main.rs` and `secure/src/main.rs` (cortex-m-rt does not program it; use `cortex_m::register::msplim::write` or inline `MSR MSPLIM`). In the secure world a STKOF UsageFault escalates to the existing HardFault (zeroize + reset) because UsageFault is not separately enabled — keep that, but add a distinct fatal-screen code so bench reproduction is possible. In the FSBL install a HardFault handler that halts with a distinctive LCD pattern (the FSBL has no secrets). Also set MSPLIM_NS to the NS stack base at handover (boot_ns.rs) — an NS overflow then faults in NS (DoS only) instead of walking into the NS USB buffers. Add a `-Z emit-stack-sizes`-derived assert that guard + max frame-sum < region.
improvements.rationale: Rust has no `-fstack-protector`; the ARMv8-M hardware stack limit is the available equivalent and costs two instructions. CLAUDE.md invariant #10 says the FSBL stack is 'bounded rather than closed'; MSPLIM converts the unproven residual into a fail-stop. Trezor programs sp_lim per task with a 256 B guard and saves/restores MSPLIM/PSPLIM on every switch.

improvements.title: Deny NS the clock and voltage levers: secure RCC/PWR/SYSCFG attribution, secure PVD (2.8 V) with zeroize-and-reset, silicon receipts
improvements.threat: RCC, PWR and SYSCFG are not attributed secure, so a hostile NS can (a) retune PLL/VOS to glitch secure crypto (clock-glitch lever without touching the board), (b) enter STOP/low-power from NS, which stops TIM2/TIM3 and therefore freezes the S-only 120 s inactivity timer and the consumption mask — a software bypass of 'NS does not control the inactivity timer', (c) disable HSI48/CRS or the OTG clock to wedge the device. Separately, a hostile USB host (or a glitch rig) can brown the rail; without a PVD the secure world keeps executing through the dip.
improvements.proposal: (1) In `sau.rs` after the GTZC allowlist: write RCC_SECCFGR (all oscillators/PLLs/PRESC/BOOST secure), PWR_SECCFGR (WUP, LPM, VDM, VB, APC secure) and SYSCFG_SECCFGR (SYSCFGSEC, CLASSBSEC, FPUSEC); add them to the exact-equality const-asserts and `verify_or_halt`, and extend `gtzc_test.rs` with RCC/PWR/SYSCFG NS-alias probes. Move every clock/power action NS performs today into the secure init (the synopsys-usb-otg `UsbPeripheral::enable()` at nonsecure/src/usb/mod.rs:41 touches RCC from NS — it must become a no-op with the secure side pre-enabling OTG+HSI48+CRS, which usb_hw.rs already partially does). (2) Arm PVD level 5 (~2.8 V) rising+falling as a SECURE IRQ at highest priority whose handler zeroizes SRAM secret caches and resets (not the SE wipe), mirroring the HardFault policy; keep BOR_LEV in the ship option-byte profile as the hardware backstop. (3) Record the silicon receipt (#80) after `lock_security_config`.
improvements.rationale: Trezor secures RCC clock sources (all but PLL3), every PWR low-power/voltage bit, SYSCFG, IWDG/WWDG and the cache registers, and arms a PVD that terminates execution on a dip. pq1's allowlist covers crypto, SE buses, UCPD1, TIM2/3, SPI1 and IWDG — but not the peripherals that control the clock and the voltage those blocks run from. #80 is already priority:high; PVD is untracked (the #21 reference is the TAMP CSS/PVD backup-domain item, not a core PVD).

improvements.title: MCU-rooted genuineness attestation over USB with SPHINCS+C10 (DHUK-derived key, factory-issued certificate) — single-algorithm answer to clones and interposers
improvements.threat: Over the wire a companion cannot tell a genuine pq1 from a clone, a reflashed unit, or an interposer MCU speaking APDU v2: FW_VERSION is a fixed 3.0.0, device_uid is 16 zero bytes, the USB serial is '0001', and the SE certificates are not surfaced through any gateway command. The user's only check is the RDP-0 pre-first-power SWD verification and the boot fingerprint; after that, the companion is origin-blind.
improvements.proposal: Add CMD_ATTEST (new INS): input = 32-byte host challenge; secure world derives a per-die C10 attestation seed as `SAES-CMAC(DHUK, "pq1-mcu-attest-v1" || TRNG-salt-from-page-127)` (final only after the RDP-2 self-lock, exactly like the SE PBS rotation), keygen + sign `sha256("pq1-attest" || challenge || fw_measurement || uid96)`, zeroize, return sig + the factory-issued certificate blob (C10-signed by a PQ1 attestation CA over the attestation pubkey + UID96, stored in a read-only page written at factory and bound at first boot). Companion verifies the chain and shows a green 'genuine' state; also replace the FW_VERSION/uid placeholders with the real build hash and UID96 so the attested fields are meaningful. Combine with the existing SE attestation so the companion checks MCU+OPTIGA+SE050 identity binding (#249/#22 triple-UID).
improvements.rationale: Trezor ships MCU attestation (ML-DSA-44 over a host challenge, key from the privileged master secret, cert via startup args) as its 'genuineness check'; Ledger's Genuine Check attests the SE. pq1 can get the same host-verifiable property without a second algorithm by reusing C10 (invariant #5 holds) and the per-die DHUK story it already relies on. Honest scope: attestation detects a replaced/cloned MCU or an interposer that cannot produce the key; it does NOT detect a passive display-bus tap (the Grand Nano X implant sat behind a genuine SE).

improvements.title: Centralise gateway policy in the dispatcher: deny-first LOCKED allowlist table, NsPtr typestate on every handler, sentinel-gate the pin-attempt-log handler, count unknown CMDs as anomalies
improvements.threat: PIN gating and pointer validation are discipline-enforced per handler (20 `pin_verified` reads across 15 cmd_* files; the `NsPtr<T>` typestate adopted by one veneer), so a new command (e.g. USB-05, OFFCHAIN_SYNC, the 2026-09 pin-attempt log) can and did land without the uniform FI shape: `cmd_pin_attempt_log.rs:23` is a production, PIN-less handler with a bare `if !validate_ns_write_ptr` — the FAIL-OUT shape HIGH-1 removed elsewhere; a single branch-skip writes 23 bytes into secure SRAM. Unknown CMDs return a soft InternalError with no counting, so a host can probe the dispatcher indefinitely.
improvements.proposal: (1) In `dispatch`/the veneers: a single `const LOCKED_OK: &[u32] = &[CMD_GET_REMAINING, CMD_REQUEST_UNLOCK, CMD_IS_UNLOCKED, CMD_GET_PIN_ATTEMPT_LOG(pending #719)]` checked deny-first through the FI sentinel before the match; handlers keep their own check as belt-and-braces but the table is the reviewed policy (mirrors Trezor ALLOW_WHILE_LOCKED). (2) Migrate every cmd_* to `NsPtr::<T>::new(addr).validate_read/write(len)` so pointer validation is type-enforced; delete the free functions once no caller remains and add a semgrep rule forbidding `validate_ns_*_ptr(` outside ns_ptr.rs. (3) Fix cmd_pin_attempt_log to `check_true_into_sentinel` + HandlerGuard and track it (untracked today; #140 covers prodtest only and still says 12 gates — now 15). (4) Unknown/forbidden CMD increments an S-SRAM anomaly counter; above N (e.g. 8 per unlock session) the device locks (zeroize, not wipe) and the reason is logged to the pin-attempt ring.
improvements.rationale: Ledger's LSB-023 root cause was per-app guards decaying; Trezor's wire layer applies deny-first filters centrally and treats an invalid smcall/syscall as fatal. pq1's threat-model.md:263 already describes the typestate as THE mechanism — making the docs true is cheaper than keeping the drift.

improvements.title: Bound unsolicited PIN prompts on a LOCKED device: physical 'press to unlock' gate before the keypad plus exponential cooldown per host request
improvements.threat: When the device is locked, every INS 0x10 pops the trusted PIN dialog and arms a fresh 120 s window; nothing bounds the rate. A hostile companion trains the user to type the PIN into unsolicited prompts (prompt fatigue), blocks NS/USB for up to 120 s per pop, and can time pops to coincide with a shoulder-surf or an EM/power capture of PIN entry. F3 idempotency only covers the UNLOCKED state.
improvements.proposal: On a host-initiated unlock while locked, paint a passive 'Unlock requested — press ✓ to enter PIN' screen; the keypad appears only after a physical button event, so the host can at most show a banner. Track `unlock_requests_since_boot` in S-SRAM and apply an exponential cooldown (1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... capped at 60 s) during which further INS 0x10 return a new `NscStatus::Cooldown` without touching the display; reset the cooldown on a successful unlock or a user-initiated (button) unlock. Apply the same gesture gate to the PendSV idle re-unlock loop so the 120 s NS/USB starvation (#700/#692) becomes user-paced.
improvements.rationale: The PIN entry is pq1's most SCA/FI-sensitive user interaction and the only secret the user ever types; letting the host schedule it is a gift to an attacker with a probe on the rail. A gesture gate costs one screen and keeps the dialog user-initiated; Trezor also pops its unlock on any host message, so this is beyond parity.

improvements.title: Signing-ceremony anomaly layer (#600) made concrete: S-SRAM intent fingerprint, 'CHANGED SINCE LAST ATTEMPT' diff page, per-session repeat cap
improvements.threat: Error-mimicry: the companion reports 'failed, sign again' and re-submits a mutated payload (recipient, amount, slot, chain) until the user stops reading; the trusted display defeats substitution but not attention exhaustion. threat-model.md:282 records 'NONE TODAY'.
improvements.proposal: Keep in S-SRAM (reset on lock) the last K=4 rendered-intent fingerprints: `sha256(dialog kind || every rendered page's bytes)` plus the decoded salient fields (to, value/amount, token, chain_id, slot) and a timestamp. On the next sign request: if a fingerprint matches within 10 min, show a 'REPEAT #n of same request' banner and after n ≥ 3 require scroll-to-end plus a 2-s hold; if the salient fields differ from the most recent attempt within the window, prepend a mandatory 'CHANGED SINCE LAST ATTEMPT: <field old -> new>' page before the normal pages. Cap identical-intent re-prompts per unlock session (e.g. 5) with a refusal that names the reason; since F-17 already limits 250 signs/session, reuse its counters. Add a QEMU e2e that mutates the recipient between two signs and asserts the diff page is rendered.
improvements.rationale: This is the one companion-substitution attack the trusted display does not address, and pq1 already has everything needed (page builders produce byte-exact pages; `ui-capture` hashes frames). Trezor's `ContinueOnErrors` stops honouring host cancellation after an error; none of the vendors render a diff — a cheap, visible 'beyond' feature.

improvements.title: Make the NS APDU router host-compilable and fuzz the composed HID->APDU->chain->GET_RESPONSE path; stand up the USB-face rig; implement-or-retract the ES0499 claims
improvements.threat: The 1274-LOC NS router (per-command dispatch, drain chunker, trailer-skeleton padding that WRITES into the forwarded payload, SW mapping, router lease) is the largest host-reachable parser in the device and has zero host tests, proptest, libFuzzer or Kani; fuzz/proof coverage stops at `shared/src/apdu_framing.rs`. The live USB stack (descriptor/SETUP/wLength abuse, reset storms, suspend, ZLP) has never been adversarially driven, and threat-model.md:373 claims DWC2 ES0499 mitigations (single-packet transfers, no CSR interleaving, FIFO flush) that do not exist in our code. NS bugs are DoS-class by design, but a pre-setup device talking to a hostile host (BitBox 2026) and a wedge that survives power-cycle are real product failures.
improvements.proposal: (1) Extract `nonsecure/src/usb/commands.rs` (+ transport state) into a `pqsigner-ns-router` workspace crate behind a small trait for the NSC calls and the HID endpoint; keep the firmware a thin shim like the secure-world re-export pattern. (2) Add a libFuzzer target that feeds random 64-B HID frames through assembler -> router -> GET_RESPONSE with a mock NSC that returns arbitrary statuses/lengths; assert no panic, lease invariants, no out-of-bounds write into CHAIN_BUF, and that the trailer-padding never grows past the per-CMD bound; enrol in ClusterFuzzLite; mutation-gate it. (3) Build the Cynthion/Facedancer rig (#590) with a scripted corpus: malformed SETUP, wLength > descriptor, interface index abuse, reset/suspend storms, ZLP on every endpoint; pass criterion = device still enumerates and signs afterwards. (4) Either implement the ES0499 single-packet/flush discipline in `usb/hid.rs`/`transport.rs` (XFRSIZ = MPSIZ, RXFFLSH on reset) or rewrite threat-model.md:373 to 'claimed-not-verified'.
improvements.rationale: Trezor's protobuf decoder and THP channel code are host-compiled Rust with bounds proofs; its HID class enforces exact-size reports, read-gated re-arming and EP0 stall on unknown requests. pq1's equivalent code is only exercised on silicon by happy-path scripts.
